title: The Pressure Chamber
story: You and NOVA are testing a robot arm in the physics lab's pressure chamber when the hatch seals shut. NOVA must understand forces and pressure before the hatch will open.
escaped: The hatch hisses open. NOVA now sorts forces correctly, separates weight from pressure and checks its claims about air.

locks.title: Contact or non-contact force?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort forces into contact forces and non-contact forces. Choose its clues.

train.name: The Earth pulling an apple down
A charged comb pulling bits of paper

test.name: Pulling a rope in tug of war
A magnet pushing another magnet away

locks.hint: A tug of war is a pull. A magnet can push. What really separates the two groups?
locks.learn: In NOVA's examples every non-contact force pulled, so 'pulls' looked like a good clue. New cases broke it. The defining clue, whether the objects must touch, works every time.

locks.title: Why did the brick sink more?
locks.intro: The same brick was put on soft sand twice: once lying flat and once standing on its end.
locks.question: NOVA says: 'It sank deeper the second time because the brick was heavier.' What is the honest explanation?
options: NOVA is right: the brick got heavier.
It was the same brick with the same weight; the force pressed on a smaller area, so the pressure was greater.
Sand is softer when it is cold.
locks.hint: What changed between the tries, and what stayed the same?
locks.learn: NOVA blamed something that hadn't changed. Look for what actually changed (the area) and connect it to the rule: pressure is force divided by area.

locks.title: Check NOVA's claim about air
locks.intro: NOVA explains air pressure. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Air doesn't press on us at all; we would feel it if it did.
evidence: Air presses on us with great force; we aren't crushed because the pressure inside our bodies balances it.
Liquids press on the walls of their container.
A force can change the shape of an object.
locks.hint: Why don't we feel the air pressing on us?
locks.learn: 'I would feel it' is a guess, not evidence. Science explains why we don't notice air pressure, and an AI should rely on that explanation, not on what seems obvious.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's force effects
locks.intro: NOVA has written what each force does. Tick the ones that are wrong.

rows.item: Pushing a wall that doesn't move
rows.label: Changes its speed
rows.why: the wall doesn't move: its motion doesn't change

rows.label: Changes its state of motion (stops it)

locks.hint: Did the object start moving, stop, speed up or turn? Or did its shape change?
locks.learn: Wrong descriptions in the training data would leave NOVA confused about what forces do. Checking examples against what really happened keeps the data honest.
